writeup: TIC 200247352 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 3.3378 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The system shows a primary eclipse with 2.67% dimming and a secondary eclipse detected at 8.1 sigma significance. The Box Least Squares detection yields a signal-to-noise ratio of 413.1, while pixel-level difference imaging confirms a peak signal-to-noise of 12.1 with a centroid offset of 12.2 arcsec from the target position. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel find. The machine learning screening score of 0.94 indicates high confidence that this represents a genuine eclipsing binary. This candidate passed all automated data quality checks without flags.
